recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-28142 unless a future work-group decision reopens broader side-effect terminology across OperationDefinition and operations narrative.
issue_request: FHIR-28142 asked to clarify the computer-science meaning of side effects in the REST operations appropriateness criteria, specifically that merely constructing and returning a transient Bundle does not count as a side effect when server state is unchanged. The issue is Published and resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by git commit 5b5349293bbdc00bf741dc84397e62803b02dbb1, which changed source/operations.html to link the term side effects and to describe modification or creation of resources not transmitted as part of the RESTful call, with invoice generation and patient-merge examples.
additional_context: source/operations.html is an active built page listed in publish.ini. Confluence minutes from 2020-11-09 show the early FHIR-I process step assigning FHIR-28142 for proposed wording, and later Zulip/Confluence searches found no conflicting discussion. A Jira neighborhood search found FHIR-18197 for OperationDefinition.affectsState, but that published issue is a separate artifact-level clarification and does not change the operations-page decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. The authoritative current source already implements the Jira resolution, so adding another explanatory note would be redundant rather than a necessary correction.
